task.description:
WF-03 Step 0.5 + Step 1 for ISS-0703, on branch feature/WF03-ISS0703-20260917 (already checked out and pushed by Step 00 -- `git checkout feature/WF03-ISS0703-20260917` if your session starts elsewhere, do not re-run git setup). This issue was discovered live during REQ-360's WF-05 UAT run against the real QA instance https://qa.bizdala.com (2026-09-17): a real Keycloak password-grant token for admin-user (realm_access.roles=["PLATFORM_ADMIN"]) got HTTP 500 with an empty body from GET /api/v1/tenants, GET /api/v1/identity/users, and GET /api/v1/health, reproducibly on retry. The identical call with the identical role one day earlier (2026-09-16) got HTTP 200 with well-formed bodies. A non-admin operator-user token against the same endpoints on the same day got well-formed 403/403/404 (not 500) -- isolated to the PLATFORM_ADMIN-authenticated path specifically. Full evidence is in test/uat-reports/uat-2026-09-17-WF02-REQ360-20260917.yaml's `new_finding_for_orch_triage` and `branch_platform_admin_lands_on_workspace_root` sections -- read it in full rather than only this description.

Step 0.5 (registry lookup): check docs/issues/ for a prior *resolved* entry with matching symptoms (PLATFORM_ADMIN-specific 500s, tenant/identity/health routes, a QA-only regression). If a clear match exists, cite it and check whether this is a recurrence of a fix that didn't hold (escalate severity to at least MAJOR if so -- it is already filed MAJOR).

Step 1 (diagnose): reproduce directly against the live QA instance, do not diagnose from the bug report's prose alone.
1. Obtain a real admin-user token: `bash ../ai-dala-infra/scripts/qa-login.sh admin-user` (relative to this repo's parent directory, i.e. c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\ai-dala-infra\scripts\qa-login.sh) -- or curl the Keycloak token endpoint directly (https://auth.qa.bizdala.com/realms/bpm-default/protocol/openid-connect/token, grant_type=password, client_id=letflow-web) if that script's output shape doesn't hand you the bearer token directly. Decode the JWT to confirm realm_access.roles=["PLATFORM_ADMIN"] before using it.
2. Reproduce: curl -i (with -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>") against GET https://qa.bizdala.com/api/v1/tenants, GET https://qa.bizdala.com/api/v1/identity/users, GET https://qa.bizdala.com/api/v1/health. Confirm the 500/empty-body behavior is still live right now (it may have already been fixed by another deploy since discovery -- state plainly either way).
3. Get an operator-user token the same way and confirm the well-formed 403/403/404 contrast still holds, to keep confirming this is PLATFORM_ADMIN-specific and not a blanket outage.
4. Trace root cause. This is a live QA deploy, not a local dev environment -- you cannot attach a debugger or read QA's live logs directly unless this repo/ai-dala-infra exposes a documented way to (check ai-dala-infra for a log-access script or doc before assuming you cannot). Absent live log access, diagnose from the code: grep lib/letflow/ for the router/controller/plug code path handling /api/v1/tenants, /api/v1/identity/users, /api/v1/health, focusing on anything that treats a PLATFORM_ADMIN-scoped token differently from other roles (a role-check branch, a cross-tenant/global-scope query, an admin-only preload or serializer). Cross-reference recent commits to main (git log --oneline -20 -- lib/letflow/ around 2026-09-16..2026-09-17) for anything touching that PLATFORM_ADMIN-specific path that could explain a regression introduced between the 2026-09-16 (working) and 2026-09-17 (broken) QA snapshots -- QA deploys track main, so a merged commit in that window is the most likely suspect; state which commit(s) you found and why they are or are not implicated, or state plainly if nothing in that window looks implicated and what that means (e.g. a QA-environment-only config/data issue rather than an application-code regression -- in which case say so, this may turn into a no_defect or instrumented outcome rather than a code fix).
5. Do NOT implement a fix yourself. Complete the handoff with your diagnosis in result.summary: root cause (or, if you cannot pin down a code-level root cause, the strongest evidence-backed hypothesis plus what would be needed to confirm it), affected files/commits, and what a fix needs to change -- or, if this turns out to not be a code defect at all (pure QA-environment issue), say that explicitly so ORCH can route this as `no_defect`/`instrumented` rather than forcing a code fix that doesn't apply. Claim this handoff by setting status to IN_PROGRESS only.
acceptance_criteria: A real, freshly-issued PLATFORM_ADMIN token was obtained and used to re-probe all three endpoints against https://qa.bizdala.com just now -- current live status (still 500, or already recovered) is stated with the actual HTTP responses quoted, not assumed from the UAT report alone
A real operator-user token's contrasting response is re-confirmed the same way

Root cause is traced to specific code (file/line/commit) if it is a code defect, OR the diagnosis states plainly and with evidence that this is not a code-level defect (e.g. QA-environment/data/config issue) if that's what the evidence shows
next_action names the correct next step: CODE-DESIGNER (if a code fix is needed) or a recommendation to close as no_defect/instrumented (if not)

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 (registry lookup): searched docs/issues/*.yaml for prior resolved entries with matching symptoms (PLATFORM_ADMIN-specific 500s, tenants/identity/health routes, a QA-only regression). Checked all 9 files matching 'PLATFORM_ADMIN' (ISS-0704, ISS-0703 itself, ISS-0700, ISS-0690, ISS-0532, ISS-0531, ISS-0389, ISS-0296, ISS-0230) -- none match: ISS-0532/ISS-0531 are frontend SPA contract bugs (health-route mismatch, tenant-slug heuristic), ISS-0389 is a missing timer endpoint, ISS-0230 is tenant-provisioning rollback design, ISS-0296 is Playwright tooling, ISS-0690 is missing QA seed data, ISS-0704 is an unrelated pagination test flake. No prior resolved entry addresses a PLATFORM_ADMIN-token-triggered 500. Not a recurrence.

STEP 1 (diagnose), live re-reproduction against https://qa.bizdala.com, done just now (2026-09-17T07:21-07:22Z):

AC1 -- obtained a fresh real PLATFORM_ADMIN token via `bash ai-dala-infra/scripts/qa-login.sh admin-user` (password retrieved live over SSH from ubuntu-16gb-nbg1-1's seeded-users.env) and a real Keycloak password-grant POST to https://auth.qa.bizdala.com/realms/bpm-default/protocol/openid-connect/token. Decoded JWT confirmed realm_access.roles=["PLATFORM_ADMIN"], preferred_username=admin-user. Re-probed all three endpoints RIGHT NOW with the properly-extracted access_token (via jq -r .access_token):
  GET /api/v1/tenants        -> HTTP 200 {"items":[{"display_name":"Default Tenant",...,"slug":"bpm-default","status":"active",...}],"next_cursor":null,"count":1}
  GET /api/v1/identity/users -> HTTP 200 {"items":[operator-user,admin-user],"next_cursor":null,"count":2}
  GET /api/v1/health         -> HTTP 404 problem+json 'the requested resource was not found' (this route genuinely does not exist -- already documented by resolved ISS-0532; not the 500 class)
  Retried GET /api/v1/tenants twice more and GET /api/v1/identity/users once more: 200/200/200, no 500 at all. THE 500 IS NOT CURRENTLY REPRODUCIBLE -- it has already recovered since the UAT-RUNNER's discovery at 01:42:41Z.

AC2 -- obtained a fresh real PROCESS_OPERATOR token the same way (operator-user). Re-confirmed the contrast: GET /api/v1/tenants -> 403 problem+json 'insufficient permissions'; GET /api/v1/identity/users -> 403 same shape; GET /api/v1/health -> 404. Matches the original UAT report's operator contrast exactly.

ROOT CAUSE, confirmed directly from the live QA app container's logs (ssh ubuntu-16gb-nbg1-1, `docker logs letflow-qa-app-1 --since 2026-09-17T01:30:00Z --until 2026-09-17T02:10:00Z`), NOT guessed from prose: the exact three crashing requests are in the log, timestamped 2026-09-17T01:40:07Z-01:40:25Z, from curl/8.14.1 at 5.251.54.107 (matching the discovering UAT-RUNNER session's own tooling/IP and exact endpoint sequence: /api/v1/tenants, /api/v1/identity/users, /api/v1/health in that order). Each crashing request's captured `authorization` header value was NOT a bearer JWT -- it was the ENTIRE raw Keycloak token-endpoint JSON response, i.e. literally `Authorization: Bearer {"access_token":"eyJ...","expires_in":300,"refresh_expires_in":1800,"refresh_token":"eyJ...","token_type":"Bearer","not-before-policy":0,"session_state":"...","scope":"email profile"}` -- the caller (whatever script issued that specific call) failed to extract `.access_token` from the token response and sent the whole JSON blob as the bearer value. Each of the three requests crashed with an IDENTICAL unhandled exception: `** (CaseClauseError) no case clause matching: 123` (123 = ASCII '{', the JSON object's opening brace, which is not valid base64url) at `(jose 1.11.12) src/base/jose_base64url.erl:136 -> (oidcc 3.9.0) oidcc_jwt_util.jwe_peek_protected/1 -> oidcc_jwt_util.decrypt_and_verify/5 -> oidcc_token.int_validate_jwt/4 -> oidcc_token.unknown_kid_retry/3 -> oidcc_token.validate_jwt/4 -> lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex:250 Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline.verify_token/1`. This uncaught Erlang exception propagates all the way up and Bandit returns a raw 500 with an empty body -- NOT Letflow's own well-formed 401 Problem+JSON that every other auth-failure branch in auth_pipeline.ex uses (see reject/4 and the {:error,...} branches around lines 180-254).

Code-level defect located: `lib/letflow/oidc/token_verifier/oidcc.ex`, `Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifier.Oidcc.verify_bearer_token/2` (lines 30-45). Its own moduledoc (lines 20-27) explicitly claims it 'never raises on a realistic failure path (unresolvable provider config, expired token, bad signature, wrong algorithm)' -- that claim is FALSE for a malformed/non-JWT-shaped raw_token (garbage that isn't parseable as three base64url segments at all, as opposed to a well-formed-but-invalid JWT). The function's `with {:ok, client_context} <- ..., {:ok, claims} <- Oidcc.Token.validate_jwt(raw_token, ...)  do {:ok, claims} end` has no `rescue`/`try` around the validate_jwt call, so an exception raised deep inside the oidcc/jose dependency chain (jose_base64url.decode!/2's `CaseClauseError`) is never caught and propagates uncaught through `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline.verify_token/1` (auth_pipeline.ex:245-254, which only pattern-matches `{:ok,...}`/`{:error,...}` tuples, not exceptions) all the way to Bandit, which serves the bare 500.

WHY EXISTING TESTS DIDN'T CATCH IT: test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs (REQ-021's suite) is configured (config/test.exs) to use `Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifierDouble` throughout -- a test stub with one fixed sentinel token, never the real `Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifier.Oidcc` adapter. Its own 'malformed token' test cases (line 224 'Bearer this-is-not-the-valid-sentinel', line 241 'Bearer garbage-token') only exercise the DOUBLE's simple string-equality rejection, not the real oidcc/jose JWT-parsing code path that actually raises. grep across test/ for TokenVerifier.Oidcc found only test/specs/REQ-134.md (a spec doc) and test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs, which has zero malformed-token cases (grep for malformed/garbage/CaseClause/rescue/try: no matches) -- that integration file only tests well-formed real Keycloak tokens (valid, expired, wrong-audience), never a non-JWT-shaped Authorization value. So the real adapter's exception path is completely uncovered by the suite.

WHY THIS IS NOT A CODE REGRESSION FROM A MERGED COMMIT, checked as instructed: `git log --oneline --all --since '2026-09-16 00:00' --until '2026-09-17 08:00'` shows commits touching lib/letflow/ in that window (d6798cf6, f8095d0f, 9fb98408, 0b02f6d9, 664436fc, 543205c7, etc.) -- none touch lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex, lib/letflow/oidc/, lib/letflow/routers/tenants.ex, identity/users routing, or health routing; they are unrelated fixes (test_parallel.sh, poller flake, PATH TOCTOU, BILIMBAGA entity types). Independently confirmed the QA app container itself has NOT been restarted or redeployed in that window: `docker ps` on ubuntu-16gb-nbg1-1 shows letflow-qa-app-1 'Up 38 hours' (created 2026-09-15T17:29:29Z), and ai-dala-infra/runs/ has no letflow backend deploy after 2026-09-15-letflow-qa-deploy-001 (only a frontend-only web redeploy on 09-16, and REQ-367's CD-to-QA-on-merge automation is still status:pending/unbuilt, so nothing auto-deploys yet). So the exact same application code has been serving QA continuously since 2026-09-15 -- there is no commit in the 09-16->09-17 window that could explain a code-level regression, because the running code never changed. Also confirmed via grep of the container's full 2026-09-16 logs: zero CaseClauseError occurrences anywhere before this exact 01:40:07-01:40:25Z window, and zero afterward through 02:10Z -- this is an isolated, one-off burst tied to these three specific malformed requests, not a standing/ongoing condition.

CONCLUSION: the 'PLATFORM_ADMIN-specific QA regression' framing in ISS-0703's filing is not quite accurate -- this was never role-specific in the sense implied (PLATFORM_ADMIN vs operator); it was specific to a single malformed-Authorization-header request sequence that happened to occur during the admin-token leg of that UAT run (almost certainly a caller-side bug in however that run captured/piped the admin token -- e.g. skipping a `jq -r .access_token` extraction step -- not examined further here since it's outside lib/letflow/'s scope and the calling script/session is not preserved). HOWEVER a real, confirmed, currently-live Letflow code defect was found in the course of this diagnosis and is NOT a QA-environment/config/data issue: Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifier.Oidcc.verify_bearer_token/2 crashes with an unhandled exception (-> raw 500, empty body) instead of returning a clean 401 Problem+JSON when given ANY malformed/non-JWT-shaped bearer token -- reachable by any client (buggy or malicious) sending garbage in the Authorization header, not just this specific JSON-blob mistake, and contradicts the module's own documented 'never raises' contract plus the auth pipeline's documented design intent (auth_pipeline.ex:241-244: 'every {:error,_reason} the verifier returns collapses to a single 401'). A fix needs to wrap the Oidcc.Token.validate_jwt/3 call (and, defensively, Oidcc.ClientContext.from_configuration_worker/4) in verify_bearer_token/2 with a rescue clause that converts any raised exception into an {:error, reason} tuple Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline.verify_token/1 already knows how to turn into a well-formed 401, and needs a regression test exercising the REAL Oidcc.Token.validate_jwt/3 path (not the TokenVerifierDouble) with a non-JWT-shaped Authorization value to prove it.

issues.title: Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifier.Oidcc.verify_bearer_token/2 crashes with an unhandled CaseClauseError (-> HTTP 500, empty body) on a malformed/non-JWT-shaped bearer token, instead of the documented single-401-collapse behavior
issues.evidence: Live QA container logs (ssh ubuntu-16gb-nbg1-1, docker logs letflow-qa-app-1, 2026-09-17T01:40:07Z-01:40:25Z): three requests (GET /api/v1/tenants, /api/v1/identity/users, /api/v1/health) each carrying Authorization: Bearer <full Keycloak token-endpoint JSON response instead of the extracted access_token> crashed identically with CaseClauseError (term: 123, the '{' byte) at jose_base64url.decode!/2, propagating uncaught through oidcc_token.validate_jwt/4 and Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline.verify_token/1 (auth_pipeline.ex:250) to a raw Bandit 500 with no body. No test in the suite exercises the real Oidcc adapter with a malformed token (test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs uses TokenVerifierDouble; test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs has no malformed-token case).

result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for a fix design on lib/letflow/oidc/token_verifier/oidcc.ex: verify_bearer_token/2 must not let an exception from Oidcc.Token.validate_jwt/3 (or Oidcc.ClientContext.from_configuration_worker/4) escape uncaught -- catch it and return {:error, reason} so Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline.verify_token/1's existing {:error,_} -> 401 Problem+JSON path handles it, matching auth_pipeline.ex's documented single-401-collapse design intent. Update the moduledoc's false 'never raises' claim once fixed. TEST-DESIGNER's regression test must exercise the REAL Oidcc.Token.validate_jwt/3 path (not TokenVerifierDouble) with a non-JWT-shaped Authorization value, fail-first against pre-fix code. ISS-0703's own docs/issues/ISS-0703.yaml should be updated at Step 5 to correct the record: the originally-suspected 'PLATFORM_ADMIN-specific regression tied to a merged commit' theory is NOT supported by the evidence (no commit in the 09-16->09-17 window touches the auth/oidc code path, the QA app container has not restarted/redeployed since 2026-09-15, and the 500 is not currently reproducible with a well-formed token) -- the real, still-live defect is the crash-on-malformed-bearer-token gap in the real Oidcc verifier, triggered here by what looks like a caller-side token-extraction mistake in the discovering run, not a role-specific code path.
